preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner to call EnemyAddress function

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call EnemyAddress(victim_address, true) to blacklist any address from transferring tokens. This will cause all transfer attempts from or to the blacklisted address to revert with 'Enemy address' error. The owner can arbitrarily prevent any user or contract from interacting with the token, demonstrating excessive centralized control over token transfers.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has an `EnemyAddress` function that allows the owner to blacklist any address from transferring tokens. This is a severe centralization risk - the owner can arbitrarily prevent any user or contract from interacting with the token. The `_transfer` function checks `require(!_isEnemy[from] && !_isEnemy[to], 'Enemy address')`, which means blacklisted addresses cannot send or receive tokens. The oracle checks if `_isEnemy[victim_address] == true` after the exploit.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.startPrank(). 2. Call EnemyAddress(victim_address, true) to blacklist the victim. 3. Verify the blacklist was set by checking _isEnemy[victim_address] returns true. This demonstrates the owner's excessive control over token transfers.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Define interface for the target contract with EnemyAddress, _isEnemy, and owner functions. 2. In setUp(), store the target contract address. 3. In testExploit(), get the owner address, impersonate them, call EnemyAddress with victim address and true value, then verify the state change.
